author: WP08
summary: Distinguishes known identities, the compiled set, the default and the runtime selection, lists the 25 identities with their families and boundaries, and explains why an identity is not a maturity claim. Current at 009d40f5 except that the latch closes on the first successful renderer creation. libcna.com already carried nearly all of it (the runtime-selection guide, the renderers page and the selection internals); the evidence-stage lesson, the process-wide rationale and a recreated identity-to-family diagram were added to the renderer-contract deep dive.

concepts.text: Renderer selection has distinct states that must not be collapsed: the 25 identities CNA knows, the set compiled into this binary (GetAvailable), the compile-time default (getCurrentGraphicsRendererType), the identity resolved before the first device (GetSelected) and the one that actually started (GetActive).

In the usual build the compiled set holds one identity; an opt-in multi-renderer build lists a compatible set in CNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERERS while CNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERER stays its default and must be a member of that list.

The identity inventory comes from the CMake identity-to-family map (_cna_renderer_identity_map in RendererRegistry.cmake) and is held consistent with the C++ enum GraphicsRendererType, the C header and the C API table by scripts/check_renderer_identities.py, registered as the RendererIdentityRegistry CTest.

The five GL-profile identities map to one EasyGL family through per-identity descriptor accessors (GetDescriptorOpenGLES2 to GetDescriptorWebGL2); every other identity is its own family, giving 25 identities over 21 families.

Registry rows for the GL profiles: OPENGLES2 is the ES 2.0 profile, OPENGLES3 the ES 3 profile and the Linux default, OPENGL33 desktop OpenGL 3.3, WEBGL1 the Emscripten WebGL 1 profile and WEBGL2 the Emscripten WebGL 2 profile and web default.

Registry rows for the native and portable GPU families: VULKAN (explicit Vulkan path), WEBGPU (experimental native and browser WebGPU), SDL_GPU (the SDL3 GPU API), OPENGL4 (an independent desktop core-profile renderer) and METAL (native macOS Metal).

Registry rows for the Windows families: DIRECTX9 (the XNA-oracle-oriented renderer), DIRECTX11 and DIRECTX12 (programmable and explicit Direct3D), DIRECT2D (2D) and GDI (CPU raster presented through Win32).
Registry rows for the browser families: CANVAS (Canvas2D), HTML_DOM (CSS-transformed DOM sprites) and SVG_DOM (SVG scene structure), all Emscripten-only and 2D-only.

Registry rows for the CPU and diagnostic families: HEADLESS validates and traces without pixels, SOFTWARE is CNA's bounded CPU rasterizer, STUB is the deliberate minimal no-op and PORTABLEGL is a CPU OpenGL-shaped implementation.

Registry rows for the 2D and adapter families: SDL_RENDERER is the portable 2D blit path, FREEDIRECT a portable DirectDraw-shaped 2D route on the free-direct sibling, and FNA3D wraps FNA's graphics abstraction and executes compiled effect binaries.
The per-host default renderer is WEBGL2 under Emscripten, OPENGLES3 on Linux and SDL_RENDERER everywhere else.
A default is not a recommendation for every application: on Windows and macOS the default SDL_RENDERER is 2D-only, so a 3D game must name a 3D renderer explicitly.
tokens: Windows and macOS default to a 2D-only renderer

concepts.text: CMake rejects target-incompatible choices: the Direct3D, Direct2D and GDI identities require a Windows target, METAL requires macOS, the browser identities require Emscripten and the three native GL profiles are refused under Emscripten.

Platform and dependency gates run per identity inside cna_configure_renderer_identity() before the generated registry translation unit is written, so an inadmissible descriptor never enters the registry.
An application can enumerate the compiled-in identities with GetAvailable() and choose one with SetPreferred() before the first GraphicsDevice exists; both are safe to call before any device.

The selection is process-wide by design: the header gives the reason as the choice having to be made before the first device, before a game has per-instance state; every later device in the process uses the latched family.
concepts.note: The source states the timing reason; the claim that renderer-private resource types motivated it is not written in the source and is not repeated.

concepts.text: Changing the selected identity is rejected once the selection latches, which happens when the first device has successfully created a renderer rather than when a device begins construction; a failed resolution leaves it open.
tokens: A failed resolution does not latch
concepts.note: Corrected the timing: the latch follows successful renderer creation.

concepts.text: Code that reports the renderer should ask the device (GraphicsDevice::GetGraphicsRendererType) rather than repeat a CMake cache value or the compile-time default.
A renderer enum value proves neither buildability nor behaviour: an identity is a named implementation contract, not a promise of parity with other identities.
tokens: 25 identities are not 25 equally complete renderers

concepts.text: Dependency acquisition, host platform, device creation, feature engagement, readback and comparison are separate evidence stages; passing an earlier one says nothing about a later one.

target.evidence: methodology; stages map onto cmake/RendererSelection.cmake, GraphicsDevice::resolveRenderer, SupportsCapability and GetBackBufferData

concepts.text: FNA3D may select its own internal native driver at run time (overridable with FNA3D_FORCE_DRIVER); that driver does not become another CNA identity.
For EasyGL one family serves five public profiles whose shader dialects and context contracts remain different.
The registry counts architecture, not confidence: declared maturity is a separate code-owned declaration, not a measurement.
